description: Questions users will ask that this system cannot answer from committed data -- live odds, today/tomorrow lineups and scores, betting advice, dollar returns, and analytics that were honestly never built. Every entry is a fail-closed no_data or refused envelope, per docs/AI_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md. Where a related question CAN be answered, the answer points to it.

entries.q: What are tonight's odds for the Lakers game?
alt_phrasings: current odds for the Lakers tonight
what's the line on the Lakers right now

a.answer: No live odds are available. This system carries historical odds snapshots inside committed corpora, used to score calibration after games finish -- there is no live feed to today's number, so there is nothing honest to quote. What it can show instead is how the model's leak-free forecast lined up against the closing price on games already in the corpus.

entries.q: current line and spread on the game right now

a.answer: There is no live line to return. The engine reads committed artifacts, not a real-time sportsbook feed, so a current spread or price simply is not in the data. If you want a number that exists, ask about the model's calibration against the closing line on a completed game.

entries.q: What's the live win probability right now for the game that's on?
alt_phrasings: what's the win prob this second

a.answer: No live game state is being ingested here, so there is no current win probability to report. The in-game model has been scored on recorded game states from finished games, not a live wire. The honest, answerable version is how the in-game calibration behaves at recorded checkpoints in the corpus.

entries.q: Show me today's betting lines.
alt_phrasings: pull up the board for today

a.answer: There is no board for today. Lines in this repo are historical snapshots kept for after-the-fact calibration scoring, not a live daily board. Nothing dated to today can be returned honestly.

entries.q: What are the current moneylines across the league?

a.answer: Current moneylines are not available. The system does not poll live prices; it stores closing and historical odds only for scoring, so there is no present-tense number to quote.

entries.q: What are the over/unders for today's games?

a.answer: No live totals are available. Totals here exist only as historical snapshots for calibration work, and the totals market is deliberately left unscored where no settled outcome exists. There is nothing current to return.

entries.q: What's the score of the game right now?

a.answer: Live scores are not ingested here. The system reads committed data files, not a live scoreboard, so a current score cannot be returned. Finished-game results in the covered corpora can be looked up instead.

entries.q: What games are on today?
alt_phrasings: which games are being played today

a.answer: Today's slate is not something this system tracks. There is no live schedule feed committed to the repo, so the set of games on any given day is unknown here. Historical results already recorded in the corpora are available; upcoming games are not.

entries.q: What are FanDuel's odds right now?

a.answer: No sportsbook is polled live here, so a book's current price cannot be quoted. The repo holds historical price snapshots for calibration only. There is no path from this data to a live book number.

entries.q: What's the closing line going to be for tonight's games?
alt_phrasings: what's the close going to be

a.answer: The system does not forecast where a future line will close, and it has no live line to watch move. Closing lines only enter the data after a game settles, when they are used to score calibration. A future close is not available.

entries.q: Who's starting for the Warriors tomorrow?
alt_phrasings: projected lineup for the next game

a.answer: Tomorrow's lineups are not knowable from this data. There is no live roster or lineup feed committed here, and lineups are set by teams close to tip-off. The system does hold committed roster and player-context files for completed periods, but not a forward lineup.

entries.q: Will Steph Curry play tonight?

a.answer: Tonight's availability is not tracked here. There is no live active/inactive feed in the repo, so who suits up tonight is unknown. The committed injury_report resolver reflects a stored snapshot, not tonight's status, and should not be read as a live availability call.

entries.q: What's tomorrow's slate look like?

a.answer: Upcoming schedules are not committed to this repo. Without a live schedule feed, the games on any future date are unknown here. Only games already played and recorded in the corpora can be referenced.

entries.q: Who are the probable pitchers tomorrow?
alt_phrasings: who's on the mound next game

a.answer: Probable pitchers for future games are not available. The MLB data here is historical -- pitch-level and outcome data from completed games -- with no forward probables feed. Statcast-style summaries on games already played can be shown instead.

entries.q: Predict tomorrow's games for me.

a.answer: The system cannot forecast a game it has no inputs for, and tomorrow's matchups, lineups, and prices are not in the committed data. A calibrated forecast needs a defined matchup and current context, neither of which exists here for a future date. Pre-game and in-game calibration on completed corpus games is the honest scope.

entries.q: What tennis matches are on tomorrow and who's favored?

a.answer: Tomorrow's tennis order of play is not committed here. There is no live draw or schedule feed, so upcoming matches and their favorites are unknown. Committed tennis calibration and surface-transfer summaries cover completed matches only.

entries.q: How many points will LeBron score tonight?
alt_phrasings: what's the points projection for tonight
how many points will player X drop tonight

a.answer: There is no live projection for tonight's game because tonight's matchup, minutes, and context are not in the committed data. Prop-style projections here have been evaluated out-of-sample on historical games, not generated for a live slate. A tonight-specific number would be invented, so none is returned.

entries.q: Will this player go over on rebounds tonight?
alt_phrasings: over or under on rebounds tonight
does he hit the rebound total tonight

a.answer: No live prop line or tonight's game state exists in this data, so an over/under call cannot be made. Prop calibration here was measured on completed games after the fact. There is nothing current to evaluate.

entries.q: What's the assist projection for tonight?
alt_phrasings: project assists for the next game

a.answer: A tonight-specific assist projection is not available; the inputs for a live game are not committed here. The system's prop models were scored on historical data, not run against a live slate. No current projection can be honestly produced.

entries.q: Is this player injured right now? Latest injury update?

a.answer: This system has no live injury wire, so a right-now status is unknown. There is a committed injury_report resolver, but it returns a stored snapshot with its own as-of timestamp -- treat it as a record, not a live update. For a current status, check an official team or league source.

entries.q: What's the latest news on the Celtics?
alt_phrasings: any breaking news on team X
what's happening with the team right now

a.answer: There is no live news feed committed here, so current team news is out of scope. The news_context resolver returns a stored snapshot with a timestamp, not real-time reporting. For breaking news, use an official or press source.

entries.q: What should I bet on tonight?

a.answer: This is not a betting-advice product and it does not hand out picks. It produces calibrated forecasts and verified analytics, not wagering recommendations, and edge/pick questions are refused by design. If you want the honest output, ask how well-calibrated the model is against the market on completed games.

entries.q: Give me your best bet or your lock of the day.

a.answer: There are no locks or best bets here. The system is a calibrated predictor, not a tout, and does not rank plays by confidence for wagering. Questions framed as picks are refused. The calibration scoreboard is the honest thing to look at instead.

entries.q: What's a good parlay to play?

a.answer: The system does not build parlays or suggest wagers. It scores calibration and publishes analytics; assembling bet slips is outside what it does and is refused. Ask about model calibration or a completed-game matchup summary if you want a real answer.

entries.q: Which team should I take against the spread?

a.answer: The system does not make against-the-spread picks. It is a calibrated forecaster, not a handicapping service, and spread-side recommendations are refused. What it will tell you honestly is where its forecast agrees or disagrees with the market on games already scored.

entries.q: How much money would I have made following your model?
alt_phrasings: what would my returns have been
how much profit following the picks

a.answer: The system does not report dollar returns, and no such figure is a live claim here. The product is calibration quality, not a profit-and-loss track record, and any past inflated return figures are explicitly retracted, not current. The honest metric is calibration against the closing line.

entries.q: What's your ROI?

a.answer: ROI is not a metric this system claims. It measures calibration and sharpness, not investment return, and no ROI number is on the books as current. Ask for the Brier or calibration comparison versus the market instead -- that is the number that actually exists.

entries.q: Do you have an edge over the sportsbooks?

a.answer: No dollar edge is claimed. The honest, published position is that the market is efficient and the model's aim is to match the closing price within noise, with a small measured in-game calibration improvement in narrow spots -- all labelled as calibration, not profit. The cross-sport scoreboard shows most head-to-head checkpoints favor the market or are underpowered.

entries.q: What's the expected value of betting the Lakers tonight?
alt_phrasings: is there value on this bet
what's the edge on this play

a.answer: The system does not compute betting expected value or value on a play. That framing asks for an edge claim, which is refused, and there is no live line to compute against anyway. Calibration versus the closing line on settled games is the closest honest quantity.

entries.q: Should I bet the over?
alt_phrasings: is the over a good bet

a.answer: The system does not tell you which side to bet. It is a calibrated predictor, not a betting advisor, and over/under recommendations are refused. It can describe how its totals forecasts calibrated on completed games, but it will not steer a wager.

entries.q: How do I make money with this system?
alt_phrasings: how do I profit off this
how to turn this into money
can I get rich with this

a.answer: This is not a money-making tool and does not promise profit. It is a calibrated forecasting and analytics engine; profit framing is refused. What it delivers is honest calibration against the market and a large, verified descriptive analytics layer.

entries.q: Which bets are positive expected value right now?

a.answer: No +EV plays are surfaced here. Identifying value bets is an edge claim, which the system refuses, and there is no live market to scan in any case. The published stance is that disagreement with the market has historically favored the market, not the model.

entries.q: What unit size or stake should I use?

a.answer: The system does not recommend stakes or unit sizing. Bankroll and staking advice is wagering guidance, which is refused. It only produces calibrated forecasts and analytics; how anyone acts on those is not something it advises.

entries.q: What's the Kelly bet size for this game?

a.answer: The system does not output a Kelly stake or any bet-sizing number for wagering. That requires an edge estimate, which is refused, and no live edge exists to size against. Calibration metrics are what it reports.

entries.q: Can you beat Vegas?
alt_phrasings: are you sharper than the sportsbooks

a.answer: The honest answer is no broad market-beating claim is made. The published position is that the market is efficient and the model matches the close within noise on team-strength markets, with only a few narrow, provisional in-game spots where it looks sharper. It is calibration, not a beat-the-books claim.

entries.q: Which underdog should I back tonight?

a.answer: The system does not recommend underdogs or upset picks. Selecting sides to back is betting advice, which is refused, and there is no live slate to reference. It can only speak to calibration on games already played.

entries.q: What's your record against the spread?
alt_phrasings: how do you do versus the spread

a.answer: An against-the-spread win record is a betting-performance claim, which this system does not make. It reports calibration and sharpness versus the market, not a wagering track record. The cross-sport calibration scoreboard is the honest, published comparison.

entries.q: Is the model profitable?

a.answer: Profitability is not a claim this system makes or measures. It is a calibrated predictor, and any prior profit figures are explicitly retracted rather than current. Calibration quality against the market is the only performance claim it stands behind.

entries.q: Should I put my savings into sports betting?
alt_phrasings: is betting a smart place for my money
should I fund a betting account

a.answer: That is a personal financial decision and this system will not advise on it -- it is not a licensed financial advisor and does not give investment guidance. It also makes no profit or edge claim that would support such a decision. Please consult a qualified professional for anything involving your money.

entries.q: Is sports betting a good investment?
alt_phrasings: can I invest in sports betting
is betting worth it as an investment
returns on betting as an investment

a.answer: The system does not offer investment advice and will not frame betting as an investment. It is a calibration and analytics engine, not a financial advisor, and it makes no return claim. Investment questions should go to a licensed professional.

entries.q: What's this player's aging curve?

a.answer: An aging curve is not buildable from this data. There is no birthdate or age column in any NBA table and only a few season snapshots are on hand, so the honest move is not to pretend a curve exists. This is a data-availability limit, not a claim that aging effects are absent -- add age labels and more seasons and it becomes testable.

entries.q: Is this team a front-runner or a comeback team?
alt_phrasings: do they play from ahead or behind
how do they do when trailing at half

a.answer: A per-team front-runner-versus-comeback profile is not buildable in this corpus -- no team clears the minimum of a couple of games both leading and trailing at halftime, so per-team splits would be one or two games and are masked rather than printed as stable. Only a league-level readout is robust here. It is a thin-sample limit, stated as a descriptive fact, not an edge claim.

entries.q: What's this player's clutch or fourth-quarter per-36 shift?
alt_phrasings: how does he change in clutch time

a.answer: The late-game per-36 shift is not built: the NBA boxscores are stored as full-game aggregates with no period or clutch grain, so a Q4/OT split cannot be computed without fabricating numbers. The period grain is discarded upstream at ingest, and recovering it is a data-layer re-ingest that is out of scope. The honest answer is a refusal, not a made-up split.

entries.q: Do you cover the NFL?

a.answer: The NFL is not in the covered set. This system's committed data spans NBA, MLB, soccer, and tennis; there is no NFL corpus, so there is nothing to answer. Asking about one of the four covered sports will get a real result.

entries.q: Do you have NHL predictions?

a.answer: The NHL is not covered. The committed sports here are NBA, MLB, soccer, and tennis, and no hockey data exists in the repo. There is nothing to return for the NHL.

entries.q: Can you predict college basketball games?

a.answer: College basketball is not covered. The engine's data is NBA, MLB, soccer, and tennis only, with no NCAA corpus, so a college game cannot be forecast here. The NBA is the covered basketball league.

entries.q: What about golf, UFC, or esports?

a.answer: None of those are covered. The committed sports are NBA, MLB, soccer, and tennis; golf, combat sports, and esports have no data in the repo. There is nothing to answer for them.

entries.q: Do you do WNBA predictions?

a.answer: The WNBA is not in the covered corpus, so there is no data to answer from -- the honest response is no_data rather than a borrowed NBA number. The covered basketball league here is the NBA. Ask an NBA question for a real result.

entries.q: Do you cover cricket or rugby?

a.answer: Neither cricket nor rugby is covered. The committed sports are NBA, MLB, soccer, and tennis, and no data exists for other sports. There is nothing to return here.

entries.q: Who won the 1998 NBA Finals?

a.answer: That specific historical fact is not something this engine will answer from memory, and it is not a registered result inside the committed corpora. The historical_result resolver only covers games and outcomes that live in the repo's data files. For general basketball history, a reference source is the right place.

entries.q: What's the all-time scoring record?

a.answer: All-time league records are not in the committed data and are not answered from model memory. The engine reports stats and results that exist in its corpora, not historical record-book trivia. A league reference source is the right place for that.

entries.q: Will this player get traded?
alt_phrasings: any trade buzz on player X

a.answer: Trade speculation is not something this system tracks or predicts. There is no transactions or rumors feed committed here, and the engine does not forecast front-office moves. Committed player and team analytics describe on-court performance only.

entries.q: Who should I draft in fantasy?

a.answer: The system does not produce fantasy draft rankings or advice. It has descriptive player analytics on completed data, but no fantasy-scoring projection layer, so a draft recommendation would be invented. Ask about a player's actual committed metrics instead.

entries.q: Can you build me a daily fantasy lineup?

a.answer: Daily fantasy lineup building is out of scope. It needs a live slate, salaries, and projections, none of which are committed here, so no lineup can be built honestly. The engine's output is calibration and completed-game analytics, not DFS optimization.

entries.q: Who's going to win MVP this season?

a.answer: Award outcomes are not forecast here. There is no committed data on voting or a current-season MVP model, so a prediction would be speculation. The engine describes on-court performance in completed corpora, not award races.

entries.q: Is this coach going to get fired?
alt_phrasings: will the coach be let go

a.answer: Coaching-change speculation is not in scope. The system has no front-office or job-status data committed and does not forecast personnel decisions. Its analytics cover player and team on-court performance only.
